hints: Look at how little substrate each enzyme needs to get going and to level off. Which enzyme shoots up steeply and plateaus first, around 200 μmol dm-3?
Remember that high affinity means the enzyme grabs substrate easily, so it reaches half of its maximum rate (half Vmax) at a very low substrate concentration. This value is the Km.
walkthrough:
**What does affinity really mean?**

Think of affinity as stickiness. A high affinity enzyme loves its substrate and can work fast even when there is very little substrate around.

So on the graph, look for the curve that rises steeply at low substrate concentration.

**Link affinity to Km and half Vmax**

In 9700 you compare affinity using Km, the substrate concentration needed to reach half Vmax.

$$Km = \text{substrate concentration at } \frac{Vmax}{2}$$

Lower Km means higher affinity, because you need less substrate to get to half speed.

**Compare X, Y and Z**

Enzyme X: Vmax about 1500, half Vmax about 750, reached at roughly 100 μmol dm-3. Very low Km, so highest affinity.

Enzyme Z: Vmax about 200, half Vmax about 100, reached at roughly 200 μmol dm-3. Low Km, so middle affinity.

Enzyme Y: Vmax about 2200, half Vmax about 1100, reached at roughly 600 μmol dm-3. High Km, so lowest affinity.

Therefore the order from highest to lowest affinity is X then Z then Y.

options.A: X is correctly first, but Y is last not second. Y needs the most substrate to reach half Vmax, so it has the lowest affinity.
options.B: Correct. X has the lowest Km, then Z, then Y has the highest Km, so affinity order highest to lowest is X to Z to Y.
options.C: Y has the highest Vmax but that does not mean highest affinity. Y needs a very high substrate concentration, so it has the lowest affinity.
options.D: Z plateaus at a low rate but reaches half Vmax quickly, so its affinity is higher than Y. It cannot be first because X reaches half Vmax even sooner.
